summary: Environment A evidence for adding Edit to the Needs Attention queue's Bible action - the eighth and last Phase 6 (Operator Ergonomics) audit gap.
auditFinding: Diagnostics Mode's Pending Suggestions panel already had a full inline Edit flow (editingId/editValue state + commands.editSuggestion). The Needs Attention queue's action model (actionsFor/handleUnifiedAction) had no equivalent - no edit action, no inline-input rendering path - even though the data Edit needs (item.summary equals the reference text for a scripture-kind item) was already present in the unified feed. See docs/phase-6-8-audit.md.
designChoice: No genuine architectural fork this phase - the target UI (reuse the existing inline edit pattern from SuggestionCard) was the only reasonable shape. The one real engineering constraint was keyboard-shortcut safety: edit had to be appended last in actionsFor('bible'), not inserted before reject, since resolveUnifiedShortcutAction maps 'R' to actions[1] positionally.

newCode.actionsTs: workspace/actions.ts: UnifiedItemAction gains 'edit'; actionsFor('bible') returns ['display', 'reject', 'edit'] - edit appended last to preserve the A/R keyboard-shortcut positions. Only bible gets it - edit_suggestion is scripture-reference-specific.
newCode.intelligenceCardTsx: New editingId/editValue/onEditValueChange/onSaveEdit/onCancelEdit props; when editingId === item.id, the action-button row is replaced by an inline input + Save/Cancel, mirroring Diagnostics Mode's SuggestionCard.
newCode.attentionQueueTsx: Forwards the same five props straight through to each IntelligenceCard - still never talks to the backend itself.
newCode.liveChurchBrainTsx: handleUnifiedAction's bible case gains an edit branch setting the exact same editingId/editValue state Diagnostics Mode's Edit flow already uses (no new state); <AttentionQueue> wired to the same commands.editSuggestion Diagnostics Mode's own Save button already calls.

actionsTestTs: edit is last, not before reject - resolveUnifiedShortcutAction maps R to actions[1] positionally

fullRegression.lint: npm run lint: same 5 pre-existing warnings as before this phase - no new ones
fullRegression.rustChanges: None - zero Rust files touched this phase, confirmed via git status, so no Rust regression re-run was needed. Fifth Phase 6.x frontend-only slice, after 6.2/6.3/6.6/6.7.

architecturalSafetyNotes: Zero new Tauri commands, zero new events, zero new database schema changes - edit_suggestion (Phase 3.5) is reused entirely unchanged.
The unified queue's Edit reuses the exact same editingId/editValue state Diagnostics Mode's Pending Suggestions panel already uses - editing the same Suggestion from either surface can never desync.
Every other unified-queue action (display, reject, accept, acknowledge, review, dismiss) is byte-identical to before - Edit is strictly additive to the bible domain's action list.
resolveUnifiedShortcutAction's A/R keyboard shortcuts are unaffected - actions[0]/actions[1] still resolve to display/reject exactly as before, verified by a new dedicated test.
